::: {.research-intro}
<p style="text-align: justify">  
  My research focuses on *Theoretical Machine Learning*, particularly stochastic optimization and sampling techniques in Bayesian learning using Markov-Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms. I work on developing scalable algorithms for collaborative learning under regularization and privacy constraints.
</p>

### [Constrained Langevin Dynamics with Singular Repulsion](/research/singular-langevin/)

With David P. Herzog

We study collision-free stochastic particle dynamics inside constrained domains. The project develops stable numerical sampling methods that treat singular repulsion directly while respecting the boundary.

[Explore the project →](/research/singular-langevin/){.research-link}

### [Decentralized Proximal Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics](/research/dpsgld/)
<p class="publication-authors"><strong>Mohammad Rafiqul Islam</strong> and Lingjiong Zhu</p>
<p class="publication-venue"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.00723" target="_blank">arXiv:2605.00723</a></p>
<p>Introduces a decentralized sampler for log-concave distributions on convex domains. Shared proximal regularization allows agents to respect constraints without exchanging private data, while non-asymptotic Wasserstein guarantees quantify both network behavior and approximation bias. Experiments show rapid posterior concentration and strong predictive accuracy.</p>

### [High-Order Langevin Monte Carlo Algorithms](/research/holmc/)
<p class="publication-authors">Thanh L. Dang, Mert Gürbüzbalaban, <strong>Mohammad Rafiqul Islam</strong>, Nian Yao, and Lingjiong Zhu</p>
<p class="publication-venue"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.17545" target="_blank">arXiv:2508.17545</a></p>
<p>Develops Langevin Monte Carlo algorithms from third- and higher-order dynamics by combining splitting with accurate integration. The resulting convergence guarantees improve dependence on dimension and target accuracy as the order increases, while numerical experiments demonstrate the practical efficiency of the higher-order approach.</p>

### [Generalized EXTRA Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics](/research/extrasgld/)
<p class="publication-authors">Mert Gürbüzbalaban, <strong>Mohammad Rafiqul Islam</strong>, Xiaoyu Wang, and Lingjiong Zhu</p>
<p class="publication-venue"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.01993" target="_blank">arXiv:2412.01993</a></p>
<p>Addresses persistent network bias in decentralized stochastic-gradient Langevin methods. Inspired by EXTRA-type optimization, the proposed sampler removes that bias in the full-batch setting and yields sharper mini-batch performance bounds, enabling collaborative Bayesian learning without centralizing agents’ data.</p>

### [GJR-GARCH Volatility Modeling under NIG and ANN for Predicting Top Cryptocurrencies](/publication/pub2/)
<p class="publication-authors">Fahad Mostafa, Pritam Saha, <strong>Mohammad Rafiqul Islam</strong>, and Nguyet Nguyen</p>
<p class="publication-venue"><a href="https://doi.org/10.3390/jrfm14090421" target="_blank">Journal of Risk and Financial Management, 14(9), 421</a></p>
<p>Combines GJR-GARCH volatility modeling, Monte Carlo simulation, value-at-risk backtesting, and neural networks to study ten major cryptocurrencies. The analysis captures asymmetric volatility and tail risk, while the neural-network forecasts closely track market prices and sometimes outperform traditional ARIMA models.</p>

### [Comparison of Financial Models for Stock Price Prediction](/publication/pub1/)
<p class="publication-authors"><strong>Mohammad Rafiqul Islam</strong> and Nguyet Nguyen</p>
<p class="publication-venue"><a href="https://doi.org/10.3390/jrfm13080181" target="_blank">Journal of Risk and Financial Management, 13(8), 181</a></p>
<p>Compares ARIMA, artificial neural networks, and geometric Brownian motion using historical daily stock prices. Against observed next-day prices, the conventional statistical and stochastic models provide closer approximations than the neural-network model, illustrating the value of comparing fundamentally different forecasting assumptions.</p>

## Course Projects  
- <a href="https://www.academia.edu/103433771/Option_pricing_techniques_A_performance_based_comparative_study_of_the_randomized_quasi_Monte_Carlo_method_and_Fourier_cosine_method" target="_blank" style="text-decoration:none">Option pricing techniques: A performance-based comparative study of the randomized quasi-Monte Carlo method and Fourier cosine method</a>  
  Advisor: <a href="https://www.math.fsu.edu/~okten/" target="_blank" style="text-decoration:none">Prof. Giray Ökten</a>
  
  <div style="text-align:justify">
    Pricing financial derivatives such as options with desired accuracy can be hard due to the nature of the functions and complicated integrals required by the pricing techniques. In this paper we investigate the pricing methodology of the European style options using two advanced numerical methods, namely, Quasi-Monte Carlo and Fourier Cosine (COS). For the RQMC method, we use the random-start Halton sequence. We use the Black-Scholes-Merton model to measure the pricing quality of both of the methods. For the numerical results we compute the option price of the call option and we found a few reasons to prefer the RQMC method over the COS method to approximate the European style options.
  </div>  
  
- <a href="https://www.academia.edu/13322836/Study_of_Runge_Kutta_Method_of_Higher_orders_and_its_Applications" target="_blank" style="text-decoration:none">Study of Runge-Kutta Method of Higher orders and its Applications</a>  
  Advisor: <a href="http://appliedmath.du.ac.bd/details-ofdr-md-abdus-samad/" target="_blank" style="text-decoration:none">Dr. Md. Abdus Samad </a>

  <div style="text-align: justify">
    This project is concerned with the study on Runge-Kutta method to apply on different order of differential equation and solve different types of problem such as initial value problem and boundary value problem in ordinary differential equation. At first we discuss about the definition and generation of differential equation specially based on partial differential equation and then definition of Runge-kutta method and the derivation of midpoint method and the formula of Runge-Kutta metod of fourth order and sixth order. We also write FORTRAN 90/95 program for different order of Runge-Kutta methods. We have solved some examples of fourth order R-K method and sixth order R-K method to get the application of R-K method. We also compared the solution of R-K method with exact solution for different step sizes. Then we have given simultaneous first order differential equation and second order differential equation and then solved them by fourth order Runge-Kutta method. At last we have discussed the boundary value problem which we have solved by fourth and sixth order R-K method. After that we have written the algorithm of shooting method and showed computer results with the difference between two answer along with percentages of error.
  </div>
